Your logic is the same one that says that political donations are equivalent to "speech." Speech means you can say what you feel and have your voice heard. Voting down is a small, easily earned privilege that acts as a nice filter against rash behaviors, brigading, swarming, etc.

Growth is not everything. The fact is that the huge quantity of users on Reddit, for example, is why the site is garbage. It's also why the site is so appealing to marketers. Guess who drove the site to those user numbers and why.

Donations are absolutely speech, and it's not just the domain of the rich. We've seen this with the rise of Patreon in which individuals support not a product or service, but a person and their viewpoints. I'm not 100% sure how I feel about this, but it's a fact that many people will purchase something or donate to boost an ideological viewpoint, sometimes when the product itself has nothing to do with that viewpoint. We traditionally think of them as buycotts and boycotts.

We can all go on the Internet and spout our opinions when we are not in the employ of someone else, but by financially supporting someone and their viewpoint, you increase the odds they can express that viewpoint full-time and refine it.

I may personally believe in something strongly, but I am going to be drowned out by someone who is able to voice their opinion on, say, a podcast, because they are financially supported by donors. If I agree with that viewpoint, I may even contribute what little money I earn because I cannot personally sustain a podcast myself due to having an unappealing voice, personality or technical skills.

You don't need money to have freedom of speech, but it sure does help.

Edit: Oh, and advertising. How could I forget? Imagine a random guy with a web site and little money. He has to walk a fine line in advertising his web site lest he be accused of spamming, unless he had more money. Then he could pay for exposure for his speech.
